truths.CP2:
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM order_lines AS ol
JOIN promotions AS pr ON pr.promo_id = ol.promo_id
WHERE pr.start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  AND pr.discount_pct >= 30
truths.CP4:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(ol.quantity * ol.unit_price_eur - ol.line_discount_eur - ol.quantity * p.unit_cost_eur)
             / SUM(ol.quantity * ol.unit_price_eur - ol.line_discount_eur), 1)
FROM order_lines AS ol
JOIN promotions AS pr ON pr.promo_id = ol.promo_id
JOIN products AS p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id
WHERE pr.start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  AND pr.discount_pct >= 30

CP1.explanation: Each step ends at one row per promotion, so nothing repeats; joining the product list and the lines in one query repeats every line once per product.

CP5.explanation: The result covers only the promoted lines with no comparison to normal weeks, so it shows the margin given up, not whether a promotion paid off or how many units it sold.
